decisions.summary: the round arbiter accepted T171's section as it stands
No time-window matcher ties a detached run (no harness ancestor, no launch line) to a builder; such a run still refuses the Stop.
decisions.why: Nothing in request.md or the spec asks for detached runs to be attributed by timing. A run with no pid ancestry and no launch line cannot be tied to a builder except by a guess. The class the matcher would serve was measured as gone: 8 detached verify-gate refusals before T164, none after, and 1 refusal since T164, which was the race fix 1 fixes (dated and with its method). FR-008 (spec-index) refuses any other backgrounded make or cargo run. Leaving these runs refused keeps the guard's existing behavior and narrows nothing the GM asked for.

decisions.summary: An unnamed depth-1 agent holds a builder slot only if its type is general-purpose; typed check agents (round-arbiter, spec-fidelity) take no slot.
decisions.why: This narrows the task line's words ('an agent whose description names no task still counts as a builder'). The exception is already implied by the accepted spec: FR-006 defines a builder as 'an agent dispatched with a task's brief, not a defined review agent'. The block should have cited FR-006; it cites only T88. The purpose test also holds. Fix 2 exists so the slot count sees the builders it missed. Counting a round arbiter as a builder would read three builders running while a builder slot was free, and let the turn end over the empty slot that T88's rolling dispatch exists to fill. The rule's reach past the two types named (every other non-general-purpose type) rests on the measurement: on the 69 slot refusals, the unnamed running depth-1 agents were general-purpose 37 times and round-arbiter 11 times, and no other type appeared (dated, /tmp/t171/slots.py).

decisions.summary: Only agents at spawnDepth 1 (dispatched by the session itself) are counted as unnamed builders; a builder's own sub-agents take no slot.
decisions.why: A builder is an agent the session dispatched: FR-006's 'an agent dispatched with a task's brief', and the block's T88 reading. A depth-2 agent works inside its builder's slot. Counting it separately would overcount and refuse nothing wrongly removed. This narrows nothing in the request or the spec.

decisions.summary: A run whose launch line names another session is Status::Session; this session's turn closes and the context line names the owning session.
decisions.why: The guard's job is that a session does not end its turn over a run it started. A refusal over another session's run is a wrong outcome (block item 12), and fixing it serves FR-013's faster builders' loop. The run is still named in the context line, and nothing in request.md or the spec asks that a session be held over another's run.

decisions.why: This is a bound on an implementation walk, labeled a CONVENTION with its reason. It decides nothing the request or the spec settles.

decisions.summary: An unchanged refusal is said in full once, then as one line 'still: <first 8 words> - unchanged since HH:MM' that is still exit 2. It is said in full again on a changed text, on a block back after a passing Stop, with no session id, or when the record cannot be read or written.

The text appears in full whenever it differs from what this session was last told, and on every failure path. The repeat stands only while that same full text was already said to this session in this block, and the block measures a 32% cut in the Stop blocks' characters. On what the block states, no fidelity is lost.

decisions.summary: The one-line repeat carries the refusal's first 8 words, a labeled CONVENTION.

decisions.summary: An unchanged refusal of the set-down and finished-run guards is said in full once, then as one line 'still: <first 8 words> - unchanged since HH:MM', still exit 2; a changed text, a block back after a passing Stop, a missing session id or an unreadable record says it in full.

Limiting it to the two guards measured as repeaters is within: the GM asked a question about hook output, not for every guard to be changed in this task. The 8 words, the UTC stamp and the record path are labeled conventions.

decisions.summary: In a landing alone, a mixed build's clear or triage is withdrawn and the claim is owed whatever claims-owed's ordinary rules find between the newest clean row in dev/claims-index.json's history (the walk) and the tree: nothing where the tree is back where that answer judged it, a triage where a section/page/code moved, a full check where the claim was rewritten or a rest lost.
decisions.why: This is the arbiter's tooling_fix for ask:mixed-build-241-claims: a mixed answer is re-judged by the landing's clean build, a mechanical clear first, and impl-drift is owed only where neither reproduces it. 'Owes nothing where the tree is where the clean answer judged it' is that mechanical re-derivation, and it matches the request's convergence rule that only a claim-changing edit re-owes a check (2026-11-23).

decisions.summary: Only the fields a triage writes are withdrawn (research, pages, section, code, core, reads, triaged, cleared, triage, build); verdict, note, date, claim and rests stay.
